title: Staying in the saddle
translation: The chancellor Tokiwai was on his way to court when he met one of the palace guards, who was carrying a letter from the emperor. The guard got down off his horse.
Later the chancellor reported him: "Guard so-and-so got off his horse while he was carrying a letter from His Majesty. How can a man like that serve His Majesty?" And the guard was dismissed.
The proper way, they say, is to stay in the saddle and hold the letter up for the minister to see. Not to get down.
original: {常磐井|ときはゐ}{相国|しやうこく}{出仕|しゆつし}したまひけるに、{勅書|ちよくしよ}を{持|も}ちたる{北面|ほくめん}あひ{奉|たてまつ}りて、{馬|うま}よりおりたりけるを、
{相国|しやうこく}{後|のち}に、「{北面|ほくめん}なにがしは、{勅書|ちよくしよ}を{持|も}ちながら{下馬|げば}し{侍|はべ}りしものなり、かほどのもの、いかでか{君|きみ}に{仕|つか}うまつり{候|さうら}ふべき。」と{申|まう}されければ、{北面|ほくめん}を{放|はな}たれにけり。
{勅書|ちよくしよ}を{馬|うま}の{上|うへ}ながら{捧|ささ}げて{見|み}せ{奉|たてまつ}るべし、おるべからずとぞ。
literal: When the Tokiwai Chancellor was going to court, a northern guard carrying an imperial letter met him and got down from his horse, and

the Chancellor later said, 'Guard so-and-so is a person who got off his horse while carrying an imperial letter; how could such a person serve His Majesty?', and (the guard) was dismissed from the northern guard.
One should hold up the imperial letter while still on the horse and show it (to the noble); one should not get down, they say.

notes.text: Usually identified as Saionji Saneuji (1194–1269), Chancellor of the Realm, named after his residence at Tokiwai. {相国|しやうこく}: a Chinese-style title for the chancellor ({太政大臣|だいじやうだいじん}).
{北面|ほくめん}: the 'north side' guards, warriors who guarded a retired emperor's palace from their post on its north side. The guard corps was set up by Retired Emperor Shirakawa around 1100.

Getting off your horse when you met a high noble was ordinary good manners. But a man carrying a letter from the emperor stands in for the emperor while he carries it, so he should not bow to a minister by getting down. The guard's politeness put the chancellor above the letter.

notes.quote: いかでか君に仕うまつり候ふべき
notes.text: いかでか … べき: 'how could he…? (He couldn't.)'. {仕|つか}うまつる: humble 'to serve'. The chancellor speaks very politely ({侍|はべ}り, {候|さうら}ふ) to the sovereign about the guard.
{放|はな}つ: 'to let go, dismiss'. In the passive: 'he was dismissed from the guard'.
べからず: 'should not'. とぞ: 'so they say', with the end of the sentence left out. Kenkō records the rule as a fact of etiquette, with no comment on how hard the punishment was.
